fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from both directions on the street.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive to maintain clear sightlines for approaching responders.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles, equipment, or debris to allow emergency vehicles to reach the residence without obstruction.
• Cut back dense vegetation bordering the access drive to allow a fire or rescue vehicle to pass without restriction.
• Mark the driveway entrance with posts or reflective delineators so it remains visible at night or in reduced visibility conditions.
• Clear an area near the residence where emergency vehicles can turn around, as the single access point does not allow a second exit route.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang directly over or touch the roof and exterior walls of the structure.
• Thin the trees clustered nearest to the structure to create open space between their canopies and the building.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against or within a few feet of the structure's exterior.
• Clear grass and low ground cover in the immediate area surrounding the structure.
• Separate shrubs from nearby trees by removing shrubs positioned beneath tree canopies adjacent to the structure.
• Thin shrubs along the driveway so vehicles, including emergency trucks, can pass through without obstruction.
• Trim overhanging tree branches along the driveway to maintain vertical clearance for emergency vehicle access.
• Keep the single access route clear of fallen branches, overgrown shrubs, and encroaching vegetation at all times.
• Remove dead grass, dry plant material, and accumulated debris from the area immediately surrounding the structure.
• Thin the tree cluster on the property to separate individual trees and reduce the density of vegetation near the structure.
• Cut back mixed vegetation growing close to any outbuildings, fences, or other structures on the property.
• Mow or cut grass across the open terrain portions of the property, particularly in areas that connect directly to the structure.
